findings.summary: Host companion lookups still split the fact: `isNativeHostUiLookup` claimed every `querySelector`, so `querySelector("#id")` before the engine became a Window-realm retained query and after it an untagged optional, where `getElementById` binds a tagged companion element. `UiProjection.lookupElementId` now feeds `isNativeHostUiLookup`, the declaration binding and the call lowering, with a companion twin of the equality test.

The "one ID selector" grammar lives beside the selector parser (`uiSelectorId`, `documentLookupId` in ui-selector.ts) instead of privately in browser erasure; the static-markup `querySelector` path drops its own `#id` regex for it.
The `{argument, idOf}` closure record is replaced by `documentLookupCallId(context, call, textOf)`, which returns the id; both erasure callers shrink to one call and one test.
The method-name test runs before `libraryGlobal`, so ordinary one-argument calls no longer resolve their receiver through the checker on this path.
`elementIdLookup` reads the literal through `stringLiteralText` instead of re-spelling it.
The `primaryCanvasIds` comment names a document lookup rather than `getElementById` alone; the tests share one `compileFound` helper; docs/ui.md states the equivalence once, in the Queries row.
